Posted November 10, 2004
Analysis by Richard Cowan Sponsored by Advanced Nutrients.

Pity the poor Canadian prohibitionists. Here they are doing their best/worst trying to block the proposed phony decrim bill, and along comes DEAland ambassador, Paul Cellucci giving them help that they would be better off without.
See
 The Next Prime Minister of Canada Talks War On Us. Looming Prohibitionist Counterattack in Canada Proves Need for International Debate On Cannabis Prohibition.

The headline in today's National Post, one of Canada's two national newspapers, says, Decriminalization will further snarl border, U.S. envoy warns.

His Excellency, the enforcer, met yesterday with the National Post's editorial board which has endorsed full legalization. Consequently, he was speaking to a group that knows that he is lying. Celucci even had to acknowledge to them that several American states had decriminalized cannabis long ago. Not that facts ever influences the prohibitionist party line.

The Post even got Marlene Jennings, the Liberals' parliamentary secretary on Canada-U.S. relations to say, We're following the lead of some of the American states.

As the article pointed out, even a spokesman for Anne McLellan, the Minister of Public Safety, acknowledged that that only about 2% of marijuana heading into the United States was Canadian-grown. Educating Ann McLellan is a major accomplishment.
See
 Canadian Health Minister Seeks Asylum In DEAland; Says Making Her Think About Medical Cannabis Constitutes Torture. In DC They Don't Allow That Sort of Thing. Thinking, That Is.
and
Time Magazine Reports BC Bud 20% Less Potent Than Four Years Ago?? Incompetent Prohibitionist Propaganda and Even Worse Journalism. As Some Reporters Die to Find the Truth Others Live to Lie.

Last April, a Quebec paper reported that Cellucci understood that the phony reform could actually make the law tougher.
See
Canadian Prime Minister Commits To Decriminalization Soon Just 23 Years After He First Said He Was In Favor. It Was A Good Idea Then, But John Conroy Thinks It May Be Dangerous Now.

Cellucci was quoted as saying " For the moment, if a person is picked up in possession of marijuana, he goes before the court and nothing happens: no fine, no threat of a prison sentence, nothing! But, if a person must pay a fine of $500, perhaps that will make it less available.

Of course, the decriminalization of the possession of small amounts would have no logical impact on availability.

Nonetheless, Cellucci claimed the bill would give the impression that cannabis is easier to get in Canada, and that would put U.S. Customs officers on high alert for smugglers, which would make things worse at the border.

If people think it's easier to get marijuana in Canada, then our people at the border are going to be on the lookout, and I think they will stop more vehicles, particularly vehicles driven by young people, whether they're citizens of Canada or the United States.

Impressions are to be the basis of border policies?
See
 Decrim Okay With Drug Czar Walters? A Gaffe or a Miracle? Lessons for Canada.They Should Also Notice Alaska.

Ironically, the rationalization behind the phony decrim bill is that criminal convictions for possessing even small amounts of cannabis keep young people from being able to enter DEAland, if anyone actually checks, which they usually don't.

C$1.2-billion in trade crosses the border daily, but most of that would be unaffected by hassling young people. Of course, whenever a Canadian is kept from entering DEAland it costs some American business money, so who is really being punished?

Irwin Cotler, the Minister of Justice, the phony civil rights activist who reintroduced the phony decrim bill last week even repeated his predecessor's groveling to Washington.
See
 Canada's New Decriminalization Bill To Be Delayed After Justice Minister's Trip to Washington, and Health Minister's Trip to the Marvelous World Of Marijuana Make-Believe. John Walters In Drag?

The Post reports that Mylene Dupere, a spokeswoman for Cotler, said that the proposed law had been discussed in detail with outgoing AG John Ashcroft, and Tom Ridge, the Czar of homeland security.
See
 Did The Drug War Claim Another 3,056 Casualties On 9-11? Ariana Huffington's Extraordinary Indictment.
and
 The Endless Cynicism of the Drug Warriors. The Drug War and Terrorism. MarijuanaNews Analysis by Richard Cowan

Wow! Isn't that exciting! Canada discusses the possible decriminalization of 15 grams of cannabis in the context of homeland security with the world's largest producer, consumer and importer of cannabis.
See
 Fantasy and Reality in UN and US Reports on The Global Drug War. The Real Numbers Are There. DEAland is The World's Largest Producer, Importer, and Consumer of Cannabis.

Both expressed a full understanding of the law, claimed Cotler's aide.

Was Ashcroft anointing himself with Crisco at the time?
See
 Religious Leaders Finally Beginning To Organize Opposition To The Drug War, A Mutiny for Mercy, But For Christians There May Be A More Compelling Reason Than They Realize.

The bill faces opposition from both sides, and may not even make it through the Commons. It then faces almost certain death in the Senate.
